articles.summary: Robinson is out, but are Aberdeen’s problems much bigger than the manager?
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 10 Nov 2026 , · 28 mins

Stephen Robinson is out at Aberdeen after a torrid start to the season, but is changing the manager really enough to solve the problems at Pittodrie? articles.title: Ethiopian food: The 15 best dishes
articles.summary: The cuisine of Ethiopia is simply delicious. These are the 15 best dishes — from tibs (pan-fried sliced beef or lamb) to fuul (stewed and spiced fava beans).
articles.body: Ethiopian food is distinctive and delicious, befitting a remarkable country with a cultural heritage that stands out from the rest of Africa. While the cuisine of Ethiopia is becoming better known, it still remains something of a secret. Eating Ethiopian-style means rethinking some assumptions you might have about dinnertime — for most of us, this means starting with eschewing cutlery and being ready to get messy fingers. The foundation of the vast majority of Ethiopian meals is injera, a giant gray spongy pancake-like bread, upon whose strangely rubbery surface are served an array of foods, including multicolored mounds of spicy stews, vegetable curries and cubes of raw meat. This mode of eating is highly communal, with everyone gathering around a large circular metal tray of injera heavily laden with food as hands go back and forth scooping up food with strips of injera torn from the edges. Like Indians, the Ethiopians aren’t shy of adding spices. One of the most common accompaniments is berbere, a spice mix containing up to 16 constituent elements including chile powder, fenugreek, ginger, garlic, cardamom and cinnamon. Beyond the endless dishes, it’s essential to try Ethiopian coffee after a meal. Ethiopia is reportedly the birthplace of quality Arabica coffee, and its coffees are praised as some of the best in the world. Here are 15 essential dishes to try: Tibs Sliced beef or lamb, pan-fried in butter, garlic and onion, tibs is one of the most popular dishes among Ethiopians. It comes in a variety of forms, varying in type, size or shape of the cuts of meat used, and can range from hot to mild or contain little to no vegetables. A particularly recommended variation is shekla tibs, in which the strips of meat arrive at your table roasting atop a clay pot stoked with hot coals — dramatic and delicious. Historically, tibs was served to pay a compliment or show respect to someone. Today it’s still viewed as a special dish, hence its popularity for commemorating special events and holidays. At the same time, though, if you walk into a rowdy bar on a Friday afternoon in Ethiopia’s rambunctious capital, Addis Ababa, it’s likely that most of the revelers will be enthusiastically ordering and eating tibs. Typically, the meat of the tibs that arrives at your table has just been cleaved from carcasses hanging outside beside the restaurant’s entrance. Don’t be put off; meat rarely comes fresher or tastier. Kitfo Made from the leanest meat, kitfo is viewed as a big treat by ordinary Ethiopians, while its nutritional powers are also praised. Similar to French steak tartare, the meat is minced and warmed in a pan with a little butter, mitmita (a stronger version of berbere) and sometimes thyme. Kitfo is typically served leb leb (warmed, not cooked), though you can ask for it to be betam leb leb (“very warmed,” which basically means cooked). Kitfo can be served with aib (like dry cottage cheese) and gomen (minced spinach), a recommended pairing making the meal even more delicious, as well as especially filling — highly recommended after a hard day’s traveling or if one is confronted with a hangover after a long night. Beyainatu The name of Ethiopia’s most popular vegetarian dish translates as “a bit of every type,” hence your injera arrives blanketed in piles of tasty and colorful vegetables, potatoes, curries, lentil stews and more, creating a riot of colors and tastes. Because of Ethiopia’s strong tradition of religious fasting and abstaining from meat on Wednesdays and Fridays, beyainatu is widely available around the country, and served just about everywhere from fancy hotels to tiny food shacks beside the road. Hence when traveling or faced with a menu only printed in Amharic, beyainatu is a safe and simple go-to. Many visitors to Ethiopia return proclaiming — regardless of whether they are vegetarian — beyainatu is their favorite meal. Fuul Popular across East Africa and the Middle East, Ethiopian fuul is a mix of stewed and spiced fava beans eaten by many Ethiopians for breakfast. Regular fuul is usually served as a modest portion for one — while still filling you up — supplemented with an endless supply of fresh bread. So-called special fuul is usually large enough to share, and served with yogurt, tomato, green chile, onion, egg and occasionally avocado. Locals mash this together and season further with salt, additional spices and fresh chiles. You can tell you are in the right sort of fuul-serving diner if it’s brought to you in small metal bowls that are too hot to touch, with eaters using a piece of torn-off bread to grip the bowl’s side. Fuul serves as a healthy fast food, especially in Addis Ababa, where it is often cooked and dispensed out of vast pots, with most customers well fed in under 10 minutes before they head off into the teeming city for their day’s work. Tere siga Not for the faint-hearted, one of Ethiopia’s most popular delicacies is cubes of raw red meat. Two people typically order half a kilo of tere siga to share, which is eaten with injera or bread to clasp the meat you carve off the raw slab, and dipped in copious amounts of mitmita. One of the stories about how Ethiopians developed a love of raw meat is that it was developed as a military tactic during the 16th century so fighters could avoid detection by not having to start fires to cook their meat. While most Ethiopians seem to suffer no adverse effects from eating tere siga — the majority avow it makes them feel on top of the world — eating raw meat does carry a relative health risk. This ranges from tapeworm to salmonella, though this author hasn’t experienced any problems post-tere siga. If you’re concerned after a trip to Ethiopia, a simple tablet available from pharmacies can be taken to neutralize any tapeworm risk. Doro wot Wot is Ethiopia’s version of curry, and the ubiquitous companion of injera. While beef and goat are often used with wot, chicken — doro in Amharic — reigns as the wot champion. Doro wot is made with chicken drumsticks or wings cooked and served in a hot sauce of butter, onion, chile, cardamom and berbere. In the midst of this stew incongruously bobs a hard-boiled egg. It proves a delicious accompaniment — typically offered to a guest as a sign of respect. For Ethiopians, doro wot is the go-to meal of celebration during national and religious festivals (the day before, women can be seen everywhere carrying upside-down clucking chickens by their feet). Enkulal firfir While basically just scrambled eggs, which might not sound that exciting, Ethiopia’s enkulal firfir is not to be missed at breakfast. Cooked with nitre kibe — Ethiopian spiced butter — it is further enhanced with a combination of green and red peppers, chile, tomatoes and onions, all of which is scooped up with fresh tasty bread rolls, often still warm from the bakery. A notable feature of enkulal firfir is how fantastically yellow it is, which translates into a far superior taste compared to the results of pallid egg yolks in the West. The omelet version is known as enkulal tibs. Be warned: your appreciation of scrambled eggs back home will never be quite the same after savoring enkulal firfir. Dulet For the uninitiated, this dish of mixed meats might be more enjoyable if not translated and explained. It’s made with minced tripe (an animal’s stomach lining), along with liver and lean beef fried in butter, onions, chile, cardamom and pepper. Like kitfo, much of its popularity stems from it being very filling and hitting the spot after a hard-going day or night. Offal has never tasted so good — give it a go. Shiro A lightly spiced chickpea or bean purée, shiro is particularly favored by Ethiopians on fasting days. One of the most unassuming dishes you’ll encounter, it can appear as not much more than slop. Don’t be deceived, it’s very tasty. Shiro is often prepared with the addition of minced onions, garlic and, depending upon regional variation, ground ginger or chopped tomatoes and chile peppers, further boosting the flavor. Tegabino shiro is a type of shiro made with heavily spiced legumes, flour, oil or butter, and water brought to the boil, and then brought bubbling all the way to the table in a miniature clay pot. Ti’hilo A specialty in Tigray, Ethiopia’s most northern region, Ti’hilo is Ethiopia’s answer to Swiss fondue, consisting of barley balls pierced by carved sticks with two prongs at the end and dipped in a fiery-looking sauce made from pulses, flour and spices. As with much eating in Ethiopia, a touch of ceremony attends this dish: A person comes and sits by your table while scooping from a triangular wedge of barley and rolling the barley between hands into little balls to be placed on the tray of injera for you to pierce, dip and eat. Having long been associated with just a small part of Tigray, around the city of Adigrat especially, the tasty and nutritious benefits of ti’hilo mean it’s now catching on and spreading around Ethiopia. Dabo firfir Comprising torn-up bits of unleavened bread mixed with clarified butter and berbere, and often accompanied by yogurt, dabo firfir is a good example of Ethiopian cooking’s ability to take something simple and do much more with it. Like shiro, it might not look much but dabo firfir is surprisingly tasty. And as another incentive, in this rare instance Ethiopians are willing to resort to a spoon or fork. Fatira A breakfast dish popular around the Horn of Africa, fatira usually comprises a thin pastry top and bottom with scrambled eggs and honey wedged in the middle. Typically served as a large portion, this perfect combination of savory and sweet can happily feed two. Fatira also comes in a street food version comprising small square pieces cooked in the open on a giant frying pan in the likes of Ethiopia’s beguiling eastern city of Harar. Accompanied by freshly brewed Ethiopian coffee, there aren’t many better ways to start a day of exploring Ethiopia. Asa Eating fish — asa — in Ethiopia is quite an experience. Typically, a fish such as Nile perch is fried and served entirely whole, the gaping mouth of jagged little teeth looking like you have a piranha on your plate. As ever, it’s eaten by hand with either bread or injera, accompanied by a fiery sauce to dip into. Bar a few bones, Ethiopians eat every bit, and justifiably so — the grilled fins are particularly tasty. Asa tibs are chunks of fish marinated in berbere spice and lime juice and then fried in sesame oil, olive oil and paprika, with grated garlic and ginger added. It’s a good option if you don’t want the hassle of picking out bones or having to contemplate the fish’s angry-looking face. Spriss Dotted all over Addis Ababa are juice houses — often not much more than a shack — serving spriss, delicious juice mixes made from the likes of avocado, guava, papaya, mango, pineapple and orange. Spriss is mixed by pouring layers of juice — typically from three fruits — on top of each other. There’s no water added, no sugar and no ice, just unadulterated pureed juice topped with a lime squeezed over the top. Some Ethiopians choose to add a squirt of a purple cordial that the author has never quite identified, though it adds a satisfyingly sweet touch. A juice is often served with a triangular wedge of sweetened bread, the combination of which serves as an effectively filling snack, especially if you opt for your glass to just be filled with pureed avocado. Spriss is extremely refreshing and a nice sweet break from all the other spicy foods. Pasta beu injera Italy’s historical involvement in Ethiopia means that if you need a break from endless injera — or if your stomach is feeling tender and you need to play it safe — help is at hand in the form of pasta beu atkilt, pasta with vegetables, being readily available all over the country. Ordering pasta beu siga — pasta with meat — will get you something resembling a tasty spaghetti Bolognese. Alternatively, if you want a quirky mix that would be sure to raise eyebrows in Italy, you could try pasta beu injera: a great dollop of pasta incongruously lumped in the center of injera. Even in this challenging instance, Ethiopians stay true to tradition: a fork is only used to cut the pasta into manageable bits, after which it is all scooped up with injera clasped between fingers, as usual. It’s considered one of the most filling meals you can get.

articles.title: Exclusive Ukrainian footage reveals new details of how Russia struck an underground shelter
articles.summary: CNN’s review of exclusive police bodycam footage, weapon fragments, eyewitness testimony and geolocated videos shows that the bombing was part of a “double tap” attack and involved a massive bunker-busting bomb. It was the deadliest Russian strike on Ukraine in 2026 and is believed to rank among the deadliest of the war.

articles.title: A fritura de Hegseth cruza os dois partidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Alvo de um processo de impeachment, secretário de Defesa americano personifica o desgaste do governo Trump após a derrota eleitoral, em medidas impopulares, acusações de abuso de poder e a condução da guerra contra o Irã.
articles.summary: Alvo de um processo de impeachment, secretário de Defesa americano personifica o desgaste do governo Trump após a derrota eleitoral, em medidas impopulares, acusações de abuso de poder e a condução da guerra contra o Irã.
articles.body:
O secretário de Guerra dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, em 3 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Tyler Tate/ AP

A impopularidade de Pete Hegseth no Congresso americano é bipartidária : o secretário de Defesa estava na berlinda antes mesmo do desastre eleitoral republicano da semana passada, mas rapidamente ele passou a ser o bode expiatório da eleição que levou à ascensão dos democratas em ambas as casas do Capitólio.

Tanto que o pedido de impeachment do chefe do Pentágono foi protocolado por um republicano, o congressista Thomas Massie, para forçar o seu julgamento político ainda esta semana, bem antes que o novo Congresso de maioria democrata tome posse, em janeiro.

Crítico de Trump, Massie foi derrotado nas primárias republicanas por um candidato apoiado pelo presidente. Embora no fim do mandato, corre contra o tempo, certo de que terá o apoio de correligionários republicanos para afastar Hegseth.

Ele fundamenta seu pedido em oito infrações, mas essencialmente busca incriminar o secretário de Defesa pela guerra contra o Irã, iniciada em fevereiro sem autorização do Congresso e apontada como a principal razão para a derrocada republicana nas midterms.

O congressista republicano atribui ainda a culpa de Hegseth pelas execuções extrajudiciais ordenadas no Caribe e no Pacífico contra supostos barcos de narcotráfico, pela captura de Nicolás Maduro e pela condução de uma guerra no Iêmen sem autorização do Congresso, entre as oito acusações apresentadas.

O julgamento conta com o apoio dos democratas, mas por razões diversas, além do seu papel crucial na guerra contra o Irã. “Pete Hegseth abusou de seu poder, minou a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e é o arquiteto da guerra imprudente e custosa que fracassou no Irã”, avalia o líder da minoria democrata na Câmara, Hakeem Jeffries.

O ex-âncora da Fox ganhou notoriedade pela controvérsia de suas medidas como chefe do Pentágono, e a lista é extensa.

Hegseth rebatizou o cargo para secretário de Guerra, protagonizou o expurgo de oficiais de alta patente, desmantelou iniciativas de diversidade no Pentágono, promoveu cultos religiosos em sua sede, bloqueou promoções de oficiais mulheres ou negros, repreendeu duramente a forma física de “generais gordos” e instituiu regras que proibiam, por exemplo, militares com barba.

“Nada de gordos, nada de trans, nada de barbudos, nada de esquisitões, nada de frouxos, nada de radicais. Apenas guerreiros”, declarou em setembro numa base militar da Virgínia. Hegseth instituiu testes para avaliar os níveis de testosterona em todos os militares a partir dos 30 anos e terapia de reposição para os que fossem diagnosticados com deficiência do hormônio.

Estas ações explicam a impopularidade do chefe do Pentágono e como ele facilmente se tornou um alvo atraente para o descontentamento. Numa pesquisa da CNN, em setembro, 66% dos entrevistados desaprovaram sua conduta à frente do Departamento de Defesa.

Entre militares da ativa e veteranos, 67% disseram acreditar que as decisões referentes às forças armadas são tomadas com fins políticos, segundo outra pesquisa, realizada pela Common Defense, e 53% revelaram que tinham a intenção de antecipar a reforma.

O pano de fundo para a fritura de Hegseth é o presidente Donald Trump . E ele rapidamente saiu em defesa de seu secretário, ao assegurar que venceu duas guerras, referindo-se à Venezuela e ao Irã. Demiti-lo seria, portanto, para Trump, a admissão de um erro de seu governo no Irã.

Tudo indica que o impeachment tem boas chances de ser aprovado na Câmara, mas seria improvável no Senado, que requer dois terços dos votos. O secretário se antecipou com um apelo fervoroso em um vídeo de 5 minutos, publicado após a derrota republicano e em meio aos rumores de que ele seria o primeiro alvo de um processo de impeachment: "Nós resistimos, nós lutamos", bradou.

articles.title: Estudante que morreu após passar mal no Enem foi socorrida pelo pai | G1
articles.standfirst: Iza Lara desmaiou no banheiro da escola em Cansanção, no interior da Bahia. Família afirma que Samu não levou adolescente para hospital.
articles.summary: Iza Lara desmaiou no banheiro da escola em Cansanção, no interior da Bahia. Família afirma que Samu não levou adolescente para hospital.
articles.body:
O irmão da adolescente Iza Lara, que morreu após passar mal durante a aplicação da prova do Enem , no domingo (8), na cidade de Cansanção , afirmou que o próprio pai foi quem prestou socorro à garota . Segundo ele, o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) não foi até o local.

"Ela foi encontrada desmaiada no chão do banheiro. Começaram a a ligar para o meu pai para ir buscar. Ou seja, em nenhum momento houve ambulância, Samu ou qualquer outra coisa. O que aconteceu foi meu pai encontrando a filha dele jogada no chão do banheiro ", disse Yuri dos Santos.

A adolescente de 16 anos era cardiopata e desmaiou após edir para ir ao banheiro do Colégio Estadual de Tempo Integral (CETI) Senhor do Bonfim, onde a prova era aplicada.

Segundo Yuri, após encontrarem Iza Lara desmaiada no local, funcionários tentaram acordá-la com o cheiro de álcool. Logo em seguida, ligaram para o pai. "Ele saiu do outro lado da cidade", contou.

A estudante foi levada até a unidade de saúde desacordada, no carro do próprio pai. O irmãoda adolescente pontuou ainda que, já na unidade de saúde, ela passou por diversas tentativas de reanimação, que não tiveram sucesso. Ao ser intubada, o óbito foi constatado.

Segundo informou o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) em nota divulgada ainda no domingo, a adolescente relatou um mal-estar durante a aplicação da prova, recebeu assistência médica e foi encaminhada para uma unidade de saúde, mas não resistiu.

No posicionamento, o órgão não detalha quem levou a menina para o hospital. O g1 solicitou posicionamento sobre o assunto para o Inep, Secretaria de Educação e Secretaria de Saúde, mas não recebeu retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O irmão da estudante contou que a primeira cirurgia de Iza Lara aconteceu quando ela ainda tinha oito dias de vida, após uma primeira parada cardíaca.

Na ocasião, a família descobriu que a menina tinha sopro cardíaco — um ruído produzido pelo fluxo de sangue quando passa pelas estruturas do coração.

🔎 O barulho, ouvido pelos médicos durante consulta, é um sintoma provocado pelo crescimento exagerado e fraqueza do coração.

Ao longo da vida, a garota ainda passou por outros três procedimentos e usava um marca-passo. Segundo Yuri dos Santos, a família se organizava para mais uma cirurgia ainda nesse ano, mas a irmã estava bem. Ela se inscreveu para o Enem para se preparar para fazer novamente quando encerrasse o ensino médio.

"Eu acredito que foi muita pressão que ela vivenciou no período da prova. Estava muito quente também, e, como era a primeira prova dela do ENEM, eu acho que ela ficou muito ansiosa, e aí começou a passar mal, na sala de aula", destacou.

O corpo da adolescente foi sepultado nesta segunda-feira, em Cansanção, onde a família mora.

Tanto o Inep quanto a Prefeitura de Cansanção lamentaram a morte da adolescente e se solidarizaram com familiares e amigos dela, em nota. No texto da administração municipal, é destaca a comoção causada pela perda da jovem.

O colégio, que é administrado pela Secretaria Estadual de Educação, também emitiu nota de pesar e suspendeu as aulas na segunda-feira , em respeito à memória de Iza Lara. O funcionamento só será retomado nesta terça (10).

articles.title: Plataforma movimenta mais de R$ 86 mil em contratos com empreendedores | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado tem 132 MEIs, 105 produtores da agricultura familiar e 33 órgãos públicos cadastrados no Contrata+Brasil. Ao todo, 16 contratos já foram firmados.
articles.summary: Estado tem 132 MEIs, 105 produtores da agricultura familiar e 33 órgãos públicos cadastrados no Contrata+Brasil. Ao todo, 16 contratos já foram firmados.
articles.body:
Órgãos públicos do Acre contrataram mais de R$ 86,5 mil de microempreendedores e agricultores pelo Contrata+Brasil — Foto: Divulgação/Sesc Sorocaba

Os órgãos públicos do Acre contrataram mais de R$ 86,5 mil em serviços e produtos de microempreendedores individuais (MEIs) e agricultores familiares por meio da plataforma federal Contrata+Brasil . Desde o lançamento da ferramenta, foram firmados 16 contratos no estado.

Conforme a Secretaria de Comunicação Social da Presidência da República, o Acre conta com 132 MEIs, 105 produtores da agricultura familiar e 33 órgãos públicos cadastrados. As contratações no estado incluem serviços de pequenos reparos, fornecimento de alimentos e ações institucionais.

👉 Entenda: O Contrata+Brasil é uma plataforma digital do Governo Federal (vinculada ao Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos) para compras públicas. O objetivo principal é conectar pequenos negócios a prefeituras, escolas, universidades e órgãos federais que precisam contratar.

Ainda segundo a Secretaria de Comunicação, em todo o país, o volume de negócios firmados por meio da plataforma ultrapassou R$ 100 milhões. Segundo o governo federal, cerca de 3 mil órgãos e entidades públicas e 45 mil fornecedores estão cadastrados no sistema.

O Contrata+Brasil permite que microempreendedores e agricultores familiares encontrem oportunidades de negócios com órgãos públicos. Os cadastrados recebem notificações pelo WhatsApp sobre serviços e produtos que estão sendo solicitados.

Depois de identificar uma oportunidade, o empreendedor pode apresentar uma proposta diretamente pela plataforma. O processo é gratuito e, após a realização do serviço, o pagamento é depositado em poucos dias. O modelo dispensa etapas complexas como a burocracia para fazer a contratação.

A ferramenta reúne oportunidades em 272 ocupações, incluindo atividades como eletricista, encanador, pedreiro, pintor, gesseiro, chaveiro, mecânico, costureiro e borracheiro. E também há serviços de gastronomia, fotografia, maquiagem, confeitaria, música e organização de eventos.

A plataforma também reúne ainda, oportunidades para produtores da agricultura familiar interessados em fornecer alimentos para órgãos públicos. O sistema integra o Programa Nacional de Alimentação Escolar (Pnae), que prevê a compra de produtos para a merenda das escolas.

Além disso, também faz parte do sistema o Programa de Aquisição de Alimentos (PAA), voltado à aquisição de alimentos produzidos pela agricultura familiar. Com isso, os agricultores cadastrados podem acompanhar oportunidades de fornecimento e participar dos processos de contratação.

Com a sanção do Projeto de Lei Complementar (PLP) nº 186/2026, pelo governo federal em 21 de outubro, ocorreu uma mudança que deve ampliar o valor das contratações do Contrata+Brasil a partir de 2027, visto que o limite por serviço contratado passou de R$ 13.098,41 para R$ 32.746,06.

articles.title: Hungria detém irmão de Viktor Orbán em investigação por tráfico de pessoas, diz primeiro-ministro | G1
articles.standfirst: Em uma publicação no Facebook, Viktor Orbán classificou a detenção de seu irmão como um caso de vingança política.
articles.summary: Em uma publicação no Facebook, Viktor Orbán classificou a detenção de seu irmão como um caso de vingança política.
articles.body:
Em 9 de novembro de 2026, carros foram vistos estacionados em frente ao conjunto habitacional onde Aron Orban, irmão mais novo do ex-líder nacionalista húngaro Viktor Orban, supostamente reside, em Fot, perto de Budapeste. — Foto: AFP

A Hungria deteve o irmão do ex-primeiro-ministro Viktor Orbán durante a investigação de um caso de tráfico de pessoas, confirmou o primeiro-ministro Peter Magyar em um discurso em Berlim.

Os comentários de segunda-feira surgiram depois que o órgão anticorrupção húngaro afirmou, em comunicado, que juntamente com a polícia, deteve quatro pessoas e realizou buscas em residências em vários locais de Budapeste e do condado de Pest como parte da investigação.

"Três dos ex-ministros de Orbán já estão sob custódia", disse Magyar à margem de um discurso na capital alemã.

"O irmão dele já foi preso hoje", acrescentou, referindo-se ao irmão do ex-primeiro-ministro, o empresário Aron Orban, de 49 anos.

Em uma publicação no Facebook, Viktor Orban classificou a detenção de seu irmão como um caso de vingança política.

"Nesse jogo sujo, o objetivo é a eliminação do adversário político e o estabelecimento de um sistema de partido único. Eu sou o alvo, meu irmão mais novo é apenas um instrumento", escreveu o ex-primeiro-ministro.

O primeiro-ministro da Hungria, Viktor Orbán — Foto: AP Photo/Denes Erdos

Na declaração de segunda-feira, o Gabinete Nacional de Proteção e Recuperação de Ativos não identificou os suspeitos detidos, e a polícia também se recusou a fazê-lo em resposta enviada por e-mail à Reuters.

O órgão foi criado para investigar alegações de corrupção durante os 16 anos de governo de Orbán, as quais este último nega.

Foi criado por Magyar, que depôs Orban nas eleições de abril, e é fundamental para a campanha anticorrupção do seu governo, que ele apelidou de "Operação Purgatório".

A declaração de segunda-feira afirmava que os quatro detidos eram suspeitos de ajudar cidadãos vietnamitas a chegar à Europa Ocidental por vários meses em 2024.

Os criminosos cobravam dos solicitantes de visto uma suposta taxa de recrutamento nas missões diplomáticas da Hungria no Vietnã, e depois dividiam o valor com os demais, disseram as autoridades.

A mulher e os três homens detidos são suspeitos "de tráfico de pessoas cometido no âmbito de uma conspiração criminosa com o objetivo de obter lucro financeiro", disse a polícia.

Em setembro, a NVVH afirmou que "vender conexões políticas para obter autorizações de residência para fins de emprego" estava entre os quatro primeiros casos que planejava investigar.

Dois ex-ministros do governo Orban e o ex-presidente do banco central, Gyorgy Matolcsy, estão atualmente presos sob acusações de corrupção em investigações separadas.

articles.title: Professora viraliza com dica: 'aprender com 40 anos é sacanagem' | G1
articles.standfirst: A repercussão surpreendeu a educadora de 31 anos, que atua na rede pública entre Teresina e Timon.
articles.summary: A repercussão surpreendeu a educadora de 31 anos, que atua na rede pública entre Teresina e Timon.
articles.body:
Um vídeo publicado pela professora Karen Ribeiro, com uma dica simples de subtração ensinada a alunos do 3º ano, viralizou nas redes sociais e surpreendeu internautas. Nos comentários, muitas pessoas brincaram ao dizer que só aprenderam a técnica na vida adulta.

Em poucos dias, o vídeo ultrapassou 5 milhões de visualizações e alcançou usuários de várias partes do país.

"Aprender isso com quase 40 anos é sacanagem", diz usuário sobre dica simples de subtração — Foto: Reprodução

Entre os comentários, uma pessoa escreveu: " aprender isso com quase 40 anos é sacanagem ".

Já outro, disse que nunca tinha visto a técnica. Em outro comentário, uma pessoas comentou que "no meu tempo não ensinaram assim".

A repercussão surpreendeu a educadora de 31 anos, que atua na rede pública entre Teresina e Timon .

Segundo ela, além da repercussão, o que chamou a atenção dela foram os comentários de pessoas que já haviam concluído a educação básica e até o ensino superior, mas afirmavam nunca ter aprendido a realizar a operação daquela forma.

"Quando percebi que o vídeo estava viralizando, fiquei em choque. Foi uma surpresa enorme. Eu jamais imaginei que uma explicação feita de maneira tão simples, como tantas outras que acontecem diariamente em sala de aula, alcançaria tantas pessoas", conta.

A explicação que conquistou a internet nasceu de uma situação comum. Karen fazia uma revisão com alunos dela quando chegou à última questão da atividade.

A estratégia usada para resolver a subtração já fazia parte da rotina de ensino dela, construída a partir da convicção de que aprender fica mais fácil quando o conteúdo é apresentado de forma clara e acessível.

"Gosto de ensinar da forma como gostaria que tivessem me ensinado: com clareza, criatividade e estratégias que façam sentido para os alunos", diz.

Professora dá aulas para alunos do 1º, 3º e 5º ano

Professora viraliza após postar vídeo ensinando estudantes a subtrair no PI — Foto: Arquivo pessoal / Reprodução

Professora há cerca de três anos, Karen leciona para turmas do 1º, 3º e 5º ano da Escola Municipal Professora Esther Couto, na Zona Sul de Teresina.

Também atua como coordenadora pedagógica da Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA) na Escola Municipal Norberto Moreira Lima, na zona rural de Timon.

Foi justamente o desejo de compartilhar experiências da sala de aula que a levou a criar um perfil no Instagram, em 2024.

Inicialmente, a página servia para registrar atividades desenvolvidas com os estudantes. Aos poucos, transformou-se em um espaço para trocar estratégias de ensino com outros educadores.

Para Karen, há uma explicação para o alcance do vídeo.

"A matemática ainda é vista por muitas pessoas como um bicho de sete cabeças. A subtração com reagrupamento costuma gerar bastante dificuldade entre os alunos. A estratégia apresentada permite visualizar a operação de uma maneira diferente e facilita a compreensão", afirma.

A professora diz que o retorno mais significativo não veio da quantidade de visualizações. Veio das mensagens de colegas reproduzindo a atividade em suas próprias salas de aula e de pais que passaram a utilizar a mesma estratégia para ajudar os filhos em casa.

"Foi muito gratificante ver professores reproduzindo a estratégia com seus alunos e pais comentando que iriam ensinar daquela maneira aos filhos. Acho que esse é o lado mais bonito de tudo isso: perceber que algo que começou dentro de uma sala de aula pode chegar a tantas outras e contribuir com a aprendizagem de tantas crianças." finalizou.

articles.title: Mineradora identifica presença de terras raras em cidade do TO | G1
articles.standfirst: Identificação foi feita em Palmeirópolis e Jaú do Tocantins, na região sul do estado. O projeto segue em fase de pesquisa e ainda será analisada a viabilidade econômica da extração.
articles.summary: Identificação foi feita em Palmeirópolis e Jaú do Tocantins, na região sul do estado. O projeto segue em fase de pesquisa e ainda será analisada a viabilidade econômica da extração
articles.body:
Pesquisa encontrou elementos de terras raras pesadas em Palmeirópolis — Foto: Divulgação/Alvo Minerals

A mineradora australiana Alvo Minerals divulgou novos resultados de uma pesquisa de sondagem que identifica a presença de terras raras em Palmeirópolis e Jaú do Tocantins , na região sul do estado. As perfurações abrangem uma área de 6,5 quilômetros quadrados.

O resultado da pesquisa foi divulgado em canais oficiais no dia 2 de novembro. Foram feitos 42 furos de sondagem que indicam uma extensão de mineralização - um perfil de argila enriquecido com elementos de terras raras pesadas - que se estende por até dois quilômetros em direção ao sul e oeste no prospecto Boa Vista, parte do projeto Bluebush.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

🔎 As terras raras são um grupo de 17 elementos químicos metálicos considerados importantes devido às suas propriedades físicas e químicas, que permitem aplicações em tecnologias, equipamentos eletrônicos, geração de energia e indústria. O Brasil tem a segunda maior reserva de terras raras do mundo, segundo o Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME).

A companhia identificou a presença de elementos como disprósio (Dy) e térbio (Tb), terras raras pesadas que possuem maior valor comercial por serem indispensáveis para motores de veículos elétricos de alta performance, turbinas de energia eólica, sistemas de defesa, aeroespacial e robótica. O ítrio (Y), presente em smartphones e computadores, também foi identificado.

A pesquisa indica ainda, um aumento na concentração desses elementos em maiores profundidades. De acordo com a mineradora australiana, mais de 100 furos adicionais aguardam resultados laboratoriais, o que poderá ampliar as descobertas geológicas sobre o depósito.

O projeto Bluebush segue em fase de pesquisa mineral, sem produção comercial ou reservas minerais comprovadas. O gerente de exploração, Júlio Liz, acompanha de perto o desenvolvimento da pesquisa nas duas cidades tocantinenses. Ele conta que a companhia deve conduzir testes metalúrgicos para analisar a viabilidade econômica da extração. Ou seja, avaliar se os custos de extração serão menores que o valor de venda dos minerais no mercado.

"Estamos bem na fase inicial. Próximo etapa é o adensamento de furos de trado em malhas. Depois, análise metalúrgica, que faz com um volume maior de amostra e gera essa análise", explica.

Com escritório físico localizado em Palmeirópolis, a Alvo Minerals possui uma "joint venture" - espécie de contrato - com a empresa Mata Azul SA, proprietária da área em que a pesquisa é realizada.

"A área é de uma empresa privada. Fizemos negócio com eles. [...] Vamos investir tudo que puder aqui. A gente tem essa filosofia, tudo que a gente puder comprar em Palmeirópolis, a gente vai. Sabe aquela coisa de tentar desenvolver à região? Sempre que podemos usar do local, a gente usa", afirma Júlio.

O Instituto Natureza do Tocantins (Naturatins) informou que a atividade realizada pela mineradora Alvo Minerals se trata de uma pesquisa mineral sem uso de guia de utilização e, por essa característica, não necessita de licenciamento ambiental. Para a atividade da empresa no Tocantins, foi emitida uma Declaração de Atividades Não Licenciáveis (DANL).

A mineradora australiana pretende apresentar sua primeira estimativa de recursos minerais em 2027, etapa que permitirá dimensionar melhor o potencial do empreendimento.

A Alvo Minerals é uma companhia australiana de exploração mineral, com atuação no Brasil e projetos voltados principalmente a cobre, zinco e terras raras. Além da Bluebush, no Tocantins, a empresa desenvolve outros projetos de pesquisa mineral no país.

Levantamento geofísico eletromagnético feito no solo de Palmeirópolis — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Alvo Minerals

Palmeirópolis fica localizada na região sul do Tocantins e faz divisa com o estado do Goiás. Fundada em 10 de junho de 1980, sua formação teve início muito antes, ainda em 1960, com o povoado de Palmeiras, nome escolhido devido aos coqueirais de babaçu existentes em abundância na região.

O município que chegou a ser um dos maiores produtores de grãos do estado de Goiás, antes de separação com a criação do estado do Tocantins em 1988.

De acordo com o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), a população estimada no município é de 7.090 pessoas. Os moradores que nascem nesta cidade são chamados de palmeiropolitano, de acordo com a prefeitura.

articles.title: Relacionamento do CEO da Nvidia com suposta espiã facilitou envio de US$ 7,5 bi em chips à China, diz site | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o The Information, Alice Huang usou contatos com a fabricante e seus distribuidores para garantir o fornecimento de chips sujeitos a restrições dos EUA.
articles.summary: Segundo o The Information, Alice Huang usou contatos com a fabricante e seus distribuidores para garantir o fornecimento de chips sujeitos a restrições dos EUA.
articles.body:
O relacionamento do CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, com uma empresária que seria espiã da China facilitou o envio de pelo menos US$ 7,5 bilhões (cerca de R$ 41 bilhões) em chips da companhia para empresas chinesas. (Entenda o caso) .

A informação foi publicada pelo site The Information nesta terça-feira (10), com base em duas fontes que conhecem a empresária.

Segundo a reportagem, Alice Huang , o marido e a irmã dela construíram uma rede de empresas na China e em Cingapura para adquirir chips da Nvidia. Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang .

No centro dessa rede estava a Shanghai Century Litong, empresa chinesa fundada em junho de 2023. Em outubro, ela conquistou o status de parceira preferencial de nuvem da Nvidia , o que lhe garantiu acesso prioritário aos chips da fabricante, informou o site.

Captura de tela do vídeo mostra o CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, e Alice Huang em um jantar em Taipei — Foto: REUTERS

Quando os pedidos de chips sujeitos às restrições de exportação dos Estados Unidos ficaram paralisados, Alice usou seus contatos com a Nvidia e seus distribuidores para garantir o fornecimento. Segundo a reportagem, ela ajudou a enviar à China cerca de 240 mil chips dos modelos H100, H200 e A100.

O conselho da Nvidia iniciou uma investigação interna para apurar se Jensen Huang, de 63 anos , foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência estrangeira. O FBI também investiga o caso .

Huang disse aos funcionários que havia sido infiel à esposa , mas não deu detalhes sobre o relacionamento . As ações da Nvidia fecharam em queda de mais de 4% na segunda-feira (9), após o início da investigação interna.

A Nvidia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário da agência de notícias Reuters.

Uma foto mostra o CEO da NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, com uma mulher confirmada por uma fonte da Reuters como Alice Huang, em Taipei, Taiwan, divulgada em 7 de junho de 2024. — Foto: IMAGENS TPX DO DIA/ REUTERS

Os EUA restringem a venda de chips avançados à China. Desde 2022, o país mantém controles de exportação para limitar o acesso chinês a esses processadores , usados para desenvolver e operar sistemas de inteligência artificial.

Alice Huang trabalhava em uma grande cliente da Nvidia . Segundo o The New York Times, ela foi executiva da Megaspeed, de Singapura, que comprou mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da fabricante em dois anos. Autoridades americanas investigaram a empresa por suspeita de ajudar a China a obter chips cuja exportação ao país é proibida.

Ela teve um relacionamento com Jensen Huang e foi apontada como agente da China . Segundo o NYT, autoridades dos EUA investigaram Alice e concluíram que ela atuava para a inteligência chinesa. O CEO admitiu à equipe, em mensagem obtida pela Reuters, que foi infiel à esposa, mas não citou Alice .

A Nvidia apura se o CEO foi alvo de espionagem . A empresa abriu uma investigação independente. Segundo a companhia, o conselho não tem motivos para acreditar que informações confidenciais ou a segurança nacional dos EUA tenham sido comprometidas. Huang afirmou que vai colaborar.

articles.title: RJ tem 705 denúncias sobre linha chilena até outubro, diz Linha Verde | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do Programa Linha Verde, do Disque Denúncia, mostram que a capital concentrou 73,5% dos registros. Dois motociclistas relataram terem sido atingidos por linhas em Teresópolis e São João de Meriti.
articles.summary: o de Janeiro registrou 705 denúncias envolvendo linha chilena neste ano, até outubro, segundo um levantamento do Programa Linha Verde, do Disque Denúncia.
articles.body:
O estado do Rio de Janeiro registrou 705 denúncias envolvendo linha chilena neste ano, até outubro, segundo um levantamento do Programa Linha Verde, do Disque Denúncia. Desse total, 518 chamadas foram registradas na capital, o equivalente a 73,5% das ocorrências.

Piedade, na Zona Norte da capital fluminense, lidera o número de denúncias na cidade, com 95 chamados. Em seguida aparece Campo Grande, na Zona Oeste do município, com 60.

Rio de Janeiro registrou 705 denúncias de casos envolvendo linha chilena até outubro deste ano — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

O risco provocado pelas linhas também é relatado por motociclistas que foram atingidos enquanto circulavam por vias do estado. Em Teresópolis , na Região Serrana, Natan Ribeiro sofreu um corte no pescoço quando passava de moto pelo bairro São Pedro.

Segundo o comerciante, o acidente aconteceu na Praça do Arruela. Ele afirmou que não havia ninguém soltando pipa no local e acredita que a linha tenha se desprendido de uma árvore.

“Não imaginei que do nada a linha ia aparecer na pista. Ela estava na parte alta ali, do nada, parece que o vento, ela desagarrou da árvore e veio na direção do meu pescoço”, afirmou Natan.

Linha chilena oferece risco para os motociclistas — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Em São João de Meriti , na Baixada Fluminense, o motociclista Anderson Clayton também foi atingido por linha chilena enquanto trafegava pela Via Dutra. Ele foi levado para o hospital e passa bem.

“Eu consegui ver a linha baixando na pista e foi o suficiente para, com a mão esquerda, tentar impedir um dano maior, mas já tinha tido um arranhão no pescoço. Eu consegui jogar a moto para o acostamento para ver o que tinha acontecido”, contou Anderson.

Motociclista ferido por linha chilena na Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Um dos equipamentos utilizados para reduzir o risco de ferimentos é a antena instalada na parte dianteira das motocicletas. O acessório é usado para interceptar linhas que estejam atravessadas no caminho dos condutores.

Apesar da proteção, nem todos os motociclistas usam o equipamento. Quem já presenciou acidentes ou foi atingido por linhas chama a atenção para a importância da antena.

“A linha chilena, quando ela pega na jugular, não tem o que fazer. Eu mesmo já presenciei e, por conta disso, não ando mais sem antena”, contou o motociclista Caio Henrique.

Antenas podem salvar vidas de motociclistas — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Em algumas lojas, as antenas podem ser encontradas por valores entre R$ 15 e R$ 30.

O guarda municipal Heron de Magalhães também relatou já ter sido ferido por uma linha.

“Eu já sofri corte de luva e dedo. E falo para todo mundo, colega de trabalho, falo para todo mundo colocar pelo menos duas antenas. Eu tive sorte que pegou no dedo”, disse.

articles.title: As European Union is suing IBM, Atos and Leonardo over missed deadlines, glitches and 'Moscow link'; companies ‘remind’ upset Europe: Don't ignore …
articles.summary: The European Union’s border technology agency has sued IBM, France’s biggest IT company Atos and Italy’s Leonardo over repeated delays in developing its
articles.body: The European Union’s border technology agency has sued IBM, France’s biggest IT company Atos and Italy’s Leonardo over repeated delays in developing its Entry/Exit System (EES). According to a report in the Financial Times, citing internal communications, EU-Lisa, which oversees the system, filed the lawsuit in Estonia in December 2025 after the consortium missed delivery deadlines and challenged warnings and financial penalties, according to the report.The biometric border system was originally due to launch in 2022 but reached full rollout only this year. Its introduction has been marked by technical problems and hours-long airport queues across Europe during the summer.Project derailed by hardware and software glitchesThe EES requires travellers from outside the bloc to register fingerprints and photographs when first entering the Schengen area. It is designed to help authorities identify visa overstayers and people wanted by law enforcement. The passport-free travel area covers 29 European countries, most of them European Union ((EU) members.Software and hardware failures have disrupted its introduction, including fingerprint scanners malfunctioning when covered in sweat. Some EU countries are still acquiring scanners, the FT reported. EU-Lisa disclosed the lawsuit in annual accounts published in July, saying that it had pursued contractual and legal remedies following delivery delays to protect its financial interests.Estonia’s Harju county court confirmed that the civil case had been filed. No hearings had taken place or been scheduled, according to the newspaper. EU-Lisa declined to discuss the proceedings but said the case had “no impact on the functioning” of the EES, which it described as fully operational across Europe. The European Commission also said the dispute concerned development delays rather than the system’s operation.Atos and Leonardo declined to comment on the legal proceedings, while IBM did not respond to a request for comment, the FT reported.IBM and Atos tell EU: You cannot forget Covid-19Correspondence reviewed by the FT shows that disagreements over delivery schedules and penalties stretch back several years. In October 2021, Atos Belgium and IBM Belgium challenged both the basis and calculation of a fine, arguing that external factors, including the Covid-19 pandemic, had caused delays.The three companies subsequently objected to revised deadlines in February 2022, arguing that the timetable was unrealistic and criticising EU-Lisa’s governance of the project. “​​Ignoring reality is not prudent and will not help to achieve the plan,” the consortium reportedly wrote.A month later, an IBM representative agreed that EU-Lisa could withhold some payments pending resolution of the damages dispute. The agency’s 2022 accounts acknowledged difficulties with the consortium and said it was assessing additional costs arising from delays, which had also affected other IT projects. The contract’s total value had already increased from €142 million to €212 million in 2021.Further delays raised hardware and software maintenance expenses. In 2023, EU-Lisa nearly doubled its annual EES budget to €40 million by moving money from other projects, according to accounts cited by the FT.The original contract expired in 2025, and a new consortium took over implementation. IBM, Atos and Leonardo nevertheless remained responsible until August, EU-Lisa said.What is fear over 'Moscow Files'The project has also faced questions about cybersecurity. It was previously reported that Atos had used its Moscow office to procure software for the border system. EU-Lisa said it had identified no security breaches. articles.title: New Ukrainian footage shows how a Russian strike turned a civilian shelter into a mass grave
articles.summary: Footage exclusively obtained from Ukraine and analyzed by CNN reveals new details of how Russia struck an underground shelter with a huge bunker-busting bomb.
articles.body: Footage exclusively obtained from Ukrainian authorities and analyzed by CNN reveals new details of how Russia struck an underground shelter in southeastern Ukraine with a massive bunker-busting bomb. The November 2 attack on a village in southern Ukraine killed more than 50 people, becoming the deadliest Russian strike on Ukraine in 2026 and among the deadliest of the war. Those killed had gathered to receive food and aid – and many of them had taken cover after an earlier strike. CNN’s review of police bodycam footage, weapon fragments, eyewitness testimony and geolocated videos shows that the bombing was part of a “double tap” attack – a military tactic in which a second strike is carried out soon after an initial attack. The second strike came after emergency workers had arrived to respond to the first airstrike and villagers had sought shelter in the underground school, which had been converted into a community center. The day before the strike, the Komyshuvakha village council announced in two Telegram posts that residents could collect bread and hygiene kits at the school between 10 a.m. and noon the next day. Barely 10 miles from the front line, the school had become a lifeline for the few hundred villagers who remained in Komyshuvakha: an aid distribution point, a medical and social services hub, and a place to sleep. Aid collection turns into a rescue operation Between 9:45 and 9:50 a.m. local time on November 2, two bombs hit the school grounds, authorities told CNN. Preliminary reports indicated that one woman was killed and another was trapped beneath a concrete slab, alive but injured. No footage of the first strike was available, but Ukraine’s interior ministry and national police gave CNN exclusive access to timestamped bodycam footage from local police officers Mykhailo Romanov and Dmytro Besedin. CNN watched the footage over Zoom with a representative from Ukraine’s interior ministry. Together, the recordings offer the clearest insight so far into how the attack unfolded. CNN could not publish most of the footage because of police concerns for the victims’ families, though police posted a short, edited clip from Romanov’s bodycam online. Besedin’s bodycam footage begins at 10:15 a.m. Buildings are heavily damaged, and rubble covers the ground. Rescuers are digging through the debris to reach the woman trapped beneath the concrete slab. A fire truck stands in the courtyard, still intact. Fourteen minutes later, Romanov’s bodycam shows elderly residents gathered outside. A bicycle’s full basket suggests some had already collected aid. One man tells a police officer he is ready to evacuate the village. At 10:32 a.m., a warning comes over Romanov’s police radio: another airstrike is headed their way. Rescuers face a choice: keep trying to save the woman beneath the slab or seek shelter underground. Seconds later, another warning tells residents to take cover. Both officers join locals at the bunker entrance and descend three flights of stairs into the underground school, where aid has been distributed. They sit in a room used by local police. A second strike hits the shelter At 10:35 a.m., both bodycams capture the sound of a blast. An orange flash fills the screens before the images fade to black. Romanov and Besedin, both community police officers for more than a decade, were killed along with two other officers, according to Ukrainian police. The recordings capture their final moments and the sounds of people in the room groaning. The bunker collapsed after the explosion, Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence service said in a statement. Six more airstrikes hit the site shortly afterward, the service said. CNN reviewed dozens of videos to reconstruct the attack and independently corroborated accounts of multiple waves of strikes. Bodycam footage shows a yellow building serving as an entrance to the underground school apparently undamaged after the initial strike, despite destruction nearby. Video filmed after the bunker strike shows the same building heavily pockmarked. Trevor Ball, a weapons technical analyst at Armament Research Services who reviewed footage for CNN, said damage to nearby buildings visible before the second strike could have been caused by smaller Russian bombs, such as the FAB-500. The bodycam footage also documents the “double tap”: a second strike after responders arrived. Two first responders were killed in Komyshuvakha, according to officials. Evidence points to a massive glide bomb Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence service identified the bomb that directly hit the bunker as a FAB-3000. The weapon weighs more than 6,000 pounds and carries more than 3,000 pounds of explosives. Russia has modernized these weapons by fitting them with guidance kits, turning “dumb bombs” into precision-guided glide bombs. The FAB-3000 is designed to target fortified underground structures such as bunkers. Videos filmed after the attack show widespread devastation and a huge crater that CNN geolocated between the bunker’s two entrances. Smoke continued to billow from the crater hours later. Footage that appears to show the blast’s epicenter reveals a path through multiple layers of concrete into the bunker. CNN exclusively obtained images and video from Ukraine’s Security Service, the SBU, showing a bomb disposal team collecting munition fragments after the strike. According to the SBU video, the crater measures approximately 30 meters by 20 meters (98 feet by 67 feet). CNN could not independently measure it because satellite imagery was unavailable. Two munitions experts who reviewed the footage said the crater’s size and the damage were consistent with a 6,000-pound bomb such as a FAB-3000. Explosive munitions expert Chris Cobb-Smith and Ball reviewed the SBU imagery. Among the metal fragments, they identified the wing of a Russian UMPK glide bomb guidance kit consistent with those attached to FAB-3000s. CNN separately confirmed that the fragment matched online photographs of such kits. Danielle Bell, head of the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, condemned the attack, noting that “the timing and location of the humanitarian distribution was well publicized.” “Either the Russian armed forces knew that there was a humanitarian distribution taking place, or they failed to take the most basic steps to find out what was happening in this village they were planning to attack. In either case, this attack seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law,” Bell said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky linked the attack to the US midterm elections. “It is very telling that all of this is happening on the day of the US congressional elections. The Russians believe that America will not notice this signal from them. But such terror must be noticed and stopped,” he said. Russia, which consistently denies targeting civilians, has not commented on the strike itself. In a statement to state media, the Russian Defense Ministry said it had attacked Ukrainian military units in the area that day. Rescuers face further attacks Volunteer first responder Vladyslav Makhovsky arrived within hours of the strikes and shared several videos with CNN. They show the fire truck destroyed and mangled bicycles among the rubble, apparently left by people who had come to collect aid. One video shows a victim receiving CPR; another shows people carrying away the bodies of those killed. “Everything was burned; even the rescue workers’ car was on fire, and the area around it looked like it had been hit by a tornado – everything was destroyed. People were screaming; some were being pulled out. There was a woman there – her arm had been torn off and she was badly injured,” Makhovsky told CNN. Smoke was coming from the entrance to the underground school, Makhovsky said. Rescuers were trying to go inside with breathing apparatus. “There was a huge crater right where the school stood, and you could see the floor slabs… it was clear that the crater and its epicenter were right on top of the underground school,” the volunteer first responder added. He told CNN that Russian drones swarmed the sky for days afterward, disrupting rescue and recovery efforts. On November 8, a drone again targeted those working at the school, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said in a statement. No one was injured, but rescue equipment was damaged, the service said. From school to humanitarian hub Built with EU funding, the underground school replaced a school destroyed in a Russian airstrike in July 2023. It opened in October 2025. Video from the school showed colorful classrooms and a room lined with beds where young children could rest. The school was intended to keep children learning despite the war. Within months, however, near-constant shelling forced children to evacuate the village, and the school closed. Local authorities converted it into an administrative center and humanitarian hub for residents who stayed, either by choice or because they could not leave. Makhovsky told CNN that, to his knowledge, the site had never served a military purpose. In footage reviewed by CNN from before and after the strikes, no military infrastructure was visible, though authorities confirmed that a military commander and a military paramedic were killed at the site. The spokesperson for Ukraine’s Southern Group of Forces told CNN that the commander, Major Vitalii Bevz, arrived at the aid distribution point “after the first explosions and was killed during the repeat strikes.” Oleksandr Zalishchuk, the military paramedic, was at the scene by chance and began helping civilians, according to a statement from his brigade. The site had already come under attack that year. In June, local media reported that five Russian first-person-view (FPV) drones had attacked construction workers distributing building materials to residents whose homes had been damaged by shelling. Komyshuvakha is one of many Ukrainian frontline villages left desolate by fighting. Many buildings had already been damaged by shelling, and most of its pre-war population of around 5,000 had left. Around 200 mostly elderly residents remained, entirely reliant on aid deliveries. The few remaining police officers and volunteers such as Makhovsky carried rifles to shoot down FPV drones, a near-constant threat. In 2023, this part of the southern front was the focus of Ukraine’s failed counteroffensive, which sought to cut Russia’s land bridge from Crimea to the Donbas. Russia made small advances in the following years but repeatedly failed to take Orikhiv, a critical stronghold less than 20 miles to the south. On November 9, rescuers were still digging through rubble in Komyshuvakha, searching for around 19 people authorities believed were trapped beneath the wreckage. Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence service said DNA samples had been collected from relatives of the missing to help identify recovered bodies. Romanov and Besedin were buried Saturday alongside the two other police officers killed in the attack, Mykhailo Buzhenko and Mykola Balanda. Their final moments, captured on their bodycams, are now key evidence in the SBU’s investigation into how a shelter built to keep civilians safe became a mass grave.

articles.title: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian boy in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israel’s military says its soldiers opened fire to prevent Palestinians from throwing stones at vehicles in Burqa.
articles.body:
Israeli forces have shot and killed a 14-year-old Palestinian boy and wounded two other teens during a raid on the village of Burqa in the occupied West Bank, according to officials.

The Palestinian Ministry of Health identified the victim on Tuesday as Moataz Iyad Daghlas and said Israeli authorities were withholding his body.

The Palestinian Wafa news agency reported that two other teenagers were wounded – a 17-year-old shot in the abdomen and pelvis and a 19-year-old hit in the hand.

The Israeli military confirmed the shooting in Burqa, which is located near the city of Nablus.

In a statement, the military said soldiers opened fire to prevent Palestinians from throwing stones at Israeli vehicles.

“The forces responded with gunfire to neutralise the threat and several hits were confirmed,” it said.

According to Wafa, soldiers detained Moataz’s father and stopped an ambulance from reaching the wounded.

They briefly held three volunteer paramedics from the Palestine Red Crescent Society who were working in the area, it reported.

The attacks come as Israeli pogroms in the occupied West Bank surge to what the United Nations has called an “unprecedented level”, following the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023 and the subsequent genocidal war on Gaza.

According to the UN, at least 1,143 Palestinians have been killed in the occupied West Bank since October 7, 2023, including 250 children.

The figure includes Palestinians killed by Israeli settlers living in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED) said 2026 is on track to be the most violent year for settler-related violence since it began monitoring the territory a decade ago. In July alone, 11 people were killed in four incidents involving armed settlers alongside Israeli forces.

Hebron, Ramallah, Nablus, Jenin, and el-Bireh have seen the worst of the settlers’ pogroms.

articles.title: Moscow summit tests Russia’s waning grip on former Soviet allies
articles.summary: The CSTO’s influence is declining as Armenia turns away, while former allies pursue independent partnerships.
articles.body:
The Kremlin’s tense relationship with Armenia will be under the spotlight at a security summit in Moscow.

President Vladimir Putin will chair a session of the Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), the Russia-dominated post-Soviet military bloc, on Wednesday.

But since February 2024, Armenia’s participation in the bloc has been frozen.

While the membership technically exists, Armenia does not participate in the bloc’s activities, having effectively boycotted it after it lost a war against Azerbaijan. Yerevan blamed the group for failing to offer meaningful support during the conflict.

Armenia “de facto doesn’t participate in the CSTO’s operations,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said last week. “What happens next will depend on the nature of the discussions within the organisation.”

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on November 5 that “our interest in the CSTO has run its course”.

During the 2020 war with Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, a region once dominated by ethnic Armenians, the CSTO failed to live up to its core principle.

Neither Russia nor other member states – Belarus and three Central Asian nations of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan – deployed troops to aid Armenia, though the CSTO’s charter envisages such aid.

Moscow also maintains two military bases in Armenia with thousands of servicemen and border guards.

Azerbaijan, which withdrew from the CSTO in 1999, used new weaponry procured from Russia for billions of dollars.

Baku’s military triumph also relied on Turkish and Israeli-made drones and a revised war playbook that reflected recent breakthroughs in warfare and military technology.

Pashinyan’s anti-Kremlin stance has been a thorn in Moscow’s side since he came to power in 2018 after massive protests against Russia-backed Armenian leaders. Yerevan is also seeking membership in the European Union.

Moves to strip Armenia of its voting rights in the CSTO amount to “a demonstrative whipping”, Galiya Ibragimova, a Moldova-based expert on Central Asia, told Al Jazeera.

“Considering that the other CSTO nations are more dependent on Russia economically or stick to the, ‘Don’t poke the tiger’ logic, they’ll keep mum or watch how a bad student is being whipped in class,” she said.

The political gauntlet that Armenia – a nation of 3 million coping with the arrival of more than 100,000 people from Nagorno-Karabakh – threw at Moscow reflects a paradigm shift in the former Soviet Union.

“Yerevan’s timing for these steps is very useful as Russia is too busy with its war in Ukraine and is to a large extent weakened by [Western] sanctions and Ukraine’s military strikes on Russian economic infrastructure, as well as a looming recession,” Alisher Ilkhamov, head of the London-based Central Asia Due Diligence think tank, told Al Jazeera.

Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 became another pivotal moment that appeared to show how ineffective the CSTO was, as none of the member states backed Moscow militarily.

Shortly before the Ukraine war erupted, the CSTO flexed its muscles in January 2022, when Russia sent thousands of peacekeepers to several Kazakh cities following massive street protests.

But Moscow’s reported failures in the Ukraine war turned Russia’s political and military might “into a myth even Russian officials and military believe in – not to mention CSTO member states,” Ibragimova believes.

She said that the Russian weapons CSTO member states can procure are sold as both “discounted” and yet “advanced”, but in reality, “are very old weapons Russia didn’t need”.

Meanwhile, the ex-Soviet nations of Central Asia and the South Caucasus find new formats of military interaction.

One of them is the Turkiye-led Organization of Turkic States, which includes Azerbaijan and three Central Asian nations.

In late September, thousands of elite servicemen from Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan and Turkiye trained in Nagorno-Karabakh and on the Caspian shore to seize ships, land paratroopers and use drones to attack and supply ammunition.

In October 2025, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan held joint drills.

Moscow also failed to convince Uzbekistan, Central Asia’s economic powerhouse with a population of 37 million, to rejoin the CSTO.

Uzbekistan left the bloc in 1999, rejoined in 2006 and suspended its membership in 2012, preferring the role of an “observer state”.

“And even though Moscow expresses its vexation with the signs of disloyalty from Eurasian nations such as Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, it is so far only limited by expressing its dissatisfaction verbally,” Ilkhamov said.

“In the near future, Moscow [will be] unable to take decisive steps to bridle the region’s somewhat disloyal nations.”

Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev tries to “compensate for his steps towards the West with demonstration of loyalty towards Moscow,” Ilkhamov said.

Mirziyoyev has attended the most important date of Moscow’s political calendar – the annual May 9 “Victory Parade” that commemorates the Soviet Union’s decisive role in defeating Nazi Germany.

He also sends Uzbek troops to joint drills with Russia – but also welcomes Western dignitaries such as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio , who visited Uzbekistan in mid-October.

“No matter how Russian officials hint to Uzbekistan that it would be good to return, it never did,” Ibragimova said.

The only “real” item on the Moscow summit’s agenda is the security situation in Afghanistan, which borders Central Asia, Ruslan Suleymanov, an associate fellow at the New Eurasian Strategies Centre, a US-British think tank, told Al Jazeera.

Russian officials have warned this year that up to 23,000 fighters from more than 20 armed groups operate in Afghanistan.

Especially dangerous is ISIL in Khorasan Province (ISKP), which operates in several Afghan provinces.

The group “actively recruits youngsters from Central Asia, especially Tajikistan,” Suleymanov said.

The group’s operations reach far beyond Afghanistan – it claimed responsibility for the 2024 attack on a Moscow concert hall that killed more than 140 people, including five children, and wounded more than 550.

This year, the CSTO states boosted security on the Afghan-Tajik border that spans 1,344km (835 miles).

“That’s why Russia and Central Asian nations take what’s happening in Afghanistan seriously,” Suleymanov said.

articles.title: The Notts County fans at the FA Cup game no-one could see
articles.summary: Thick fog left Notts County fans unable to see parts of the Magpies' FA Cup win over Altrincham.
articles.body:
For many football fans, an FA Cup win is the stuff of dreams. But for 690 Notts County supporters, thick fog meant they could barely see it happen.

Ian Kirke was among the Magpies fans whose view of Saturday's FA Cup first-round tie against Altrincham was obscured by fog, leaving many unable to see the League One side's penalty shootout victory.

The thick layer of fog provided chaos not just for the players and fans, but also commentators and camera operators at the J Davidson Stadium.

Kirke said fans had to rely on the cheers - or silence - from the home support during the shootout. "It's the most bonkers festival of football I've ever seen in my life," he added.

Lifelong fan Kirke, who lives in Berkshire, said the weather at kick-off was "like any normal match".

Before fog descended over Greater Manchester, Jacob Bedeau had given Notts County the lead just before the half-hour mark.

The hosts, who play in the National League, hit back as Lucas Weaver and Lewis Banks scored to give Altrincham a 2-1 lead.

With the conditions worsening, referee David Rock opted to continue with the tie, which saw the camera often unable to pick up the ball.

The referee's decision to continue the game paid off for Notts County, who levelled the tie at 2-2, when Callum Roberts scored from the edge of the box.

"I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell.

Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard was also commentating on BBC Radio Nottingham, and said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot the ball competition.

"We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners."

Fellow Magpies fan Lynda Lally, from Beeston in Nottinghamshire, said the weather got "worse and worse" after half-time.

"For the other 45 minutes, we could only see what was happening once players emerged from the fog," she said.

The weather became "a cross between an eerie Christmas nativity gone horribly wrong - and the 1980s film called The Fog," Kirke said.

Kirke added the fog that led to an FA Cup third-round replay between Notts County and Wimbledon being abandoned in 2001 "wasn't as bad" as it was at Altrincham.

"I don't know what on earth had to happen for the referee to call it off," he said.

With the game going to penalties, Lally had hoped the shootout would take place in front of the Notts County fans so she could finally see the ball.

"Once we found out it wasn't, we were thinking what is going to happen because we can't see anything," she said.

"There was a deathly silence amongst the Notts fans when Altrincham fans at the other end were excited, and when they went silent, we went wild."

Kirke said his friend, who was struggling to see the action on TV, texted him updates during the penalty shootout.

"The only way we could ascertain what was going on was the reaction of the Altrincham fans," he said.

The sound of disappointment echoed around the stadium as Altrincham missed the target three times, before Rosaire Longelo slotted home the decisive penalty to seal a 3-2 shootout victory for Notts County.

"We heard the silence and we went into a massive roar knowing we had won," Lally added.

articles.title: Scunthorpe wildlife charity seeks funds for bigger home
articles.summary: Laxey House Wildlife Rescue in Scunthorpe says it has outgrown its current premises.
articles.body:
A wildlife rescue charity has appealed for donations to help it move to a bigger home.

Laxey House Wildlife Rescue in Scunthorpe, North Lincolnshire, was founded in 2022 and rehabilitates injured native wildlife to release back into the wild.

Chair and founder Tara Gough said the charity had outgrown its current premises, having taken in almost 1,000 animals this year so far, compared to 530 during the whole of 2024.

"Please just get behind us, share the posts, visit the website, see if there's anything that you can do to get involved," she said. "We just need that community support behind us, I think, to really drive it forward."

She said the charity had secured a lease for some land, but required more to be able to meet demand and secure a place for its hospital.

Gough said the move "needs to happen" or the centre would have to close.

"Everything just feels so heavy, it's overwhelming," she added.

"It feels unfair of me to constantly be like, we need this, when there's people struggling on a daily basis."

However, she said she believed the charity had had "such an impact" on the wildlife in Scunthorpe.

"We're providing a reliable, ethical rehabilitation service. We're knowledgeable and we've got the skills and experience to deal with species.

"If we didn't exist, I don't know what would have happened to those thousand animals."

articles.title: South Cambridgeshire projects given £1m to tackle climate change
articles.summary: South Cambridgeshire District Council says it has awarded money to 110 community projects since 2019.
articles.body:
More than £1m has been allocated to community projects tackling climate change, including solar panels for an arts centre, a bike recycling scheme and a repair cafe.

South Cambridgeshire District Council has awarded money to 110 community projects since the scheme was launched in 2019. This year £171,000 is being awarded to 14 groups, out of 37 applicants.

The Wysing Arts Centre in Bourn, Cambridgeshire, recently installed 32 solar panels, four air source heat pumps, electric vehicle charging points and a 7,500-litre rainwater harvesting tank, part funded by the scheme.

Director Rosie Cooper said: "I'm thrilled to see this project completed and already making such a difference."

The Wysing Arts Centre's projects cost £151,000, with £15,000 of this coming from the district council and the remainder from Arts Council England, Cambridgeshire County Council, the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority, Thalia and Garfield Weston Foundation.

The centre said savings generated by the improvements at its 11-acre site would be reinvested in free workshops and skills programmes for young people.

Cooper said: "It's an incredibly difficult time for cultural organisations, and we're incredibly grateful to all the partners and funders who helped make this landmark project possible."

Elsewhere, villagers in Harston raised £6,000 through cake sales, coffee mornings and quiz nights before securing a further £12,500 grant for solar panels and battery storage at the village hall.

A repair cafe, Cambridge Carbon Footprint, received £15,000 towards a project costing nearly £50,000 to encourage new volunteer groups and improve access to skilled repairers.

Cam Valley Forum received £6,000 towards making a short film, titled The Cambridge Water Crisis: How We Can All Help, aimed at encouraging residents to reduce water consumption.

Applications for the latest round of Zero Carbon Communities grant fund rose from 23 last year to 37 this year, according to council papers.

There have been eight funding rounds which were awarded on two grounds: carbon emissions reduction, or community engagement on climate change.

A report being discussed by councillors on Tuesday said: "The grant programme provides support for community climate action, in line with the council's commitment to assist communities, including promotion of sustainable behavioural change, reduced reliance on fossil fuels, increased resilience and adaptation, and the transition to net zero."

articles.title: Jersey's £10m new airport departure lounge to open soon
articles.summary: Jersey's new departure lounge features Jèrriais signage, giant wicker cows and local granite.
articles.body:
Jersey Airport's newly refurbished £10m departure lounge will finally be seen by members of the public "as early as next week", Ports of Jersey's chief executive has said.

The hall includes a viewing platform, wicker cows, Jersey granite and signage in the island's native language Jèrriais.

Matt Thomas said the re-design had been paid for solely with revenues generated by the island's ports.

Thomas said more than 100 companies and more than 1,000 people had been involved in the refurbishment project, while the designs had been informed by a public consultation.

He said: "We asked a lot of islanders 'what do you love about the island?' What came through really strongly is, 'we want to celebrate Jersey's land.'"

"So you think hedgerows, wooded lanes, wildlife, and we've tried to bring those through, but not in a gimmicky way, just in a very authentic and subtle way."

The new departure lounge also includes a family area which was designed with charity Brighter Futures, a quiet space where passengers can work and a duty free shopping area.

The next phase is due to include more shops, a sensory room and a new assisted travel lounge.

Thomas also said a single bar and restaurant would open during the next phase, and more food and beverage outlets could in future be created in the mezzanine level.

He said that the £10m spend had also included investment in new heating, flooring, air conditioning and power supplies.

"We have not had a penny of taxpayer support since we were created in 2015. So this is all from the revenues we generate," he added.

"But we're very, very confident that there's going to be amazing duty free and restaurant here - so it's actually going to pay for itself, which again, it's great for islanders."

As part of the redevelopment project, changes - including the introduction of a new parking area - have been made to the parking layout at the airport.

But after these came into effect in September, some islanders questioned the visibility of signs and the transparency of charges.

Thomas said communication of the changes could have been better.

"We don't get everything right first time," he said.

"The challenge we're trying to solve is more people are flying through the airport, we're running out of space, so we will be creating more space."

Thomas added: "Honestly...this is better than any UK airport now."

He added: "I defy anyone to come here and not be charmed."
