articles.title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's 'common sense regulation' loses support of Democratic New York City Councilman in the fear that it may make 'unhappy' Amazon go for ...
articles.summary: A New York City Democratic councilman has withdrawn his support for a controversial labour bill backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, citing concerns that the
articles.body: A New York City Democratic councilman has withdrawn his support for a controversial labour bill backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, citing concerns that the measure could lead to business closures and significant job losses, according to a report by the New York Post. Queens Councilman Phil Wong recently removed his name as a co-sponsor of the Delivery Protection Act after meeting with small business owners and logistics operators who warned that the legislation could have serious economic consequences. The bill, introduced by fellow Queens Democrat Tiffany Cabán, seeks to overhaul employment practices for "last-mile" delivery workers by requiring companies such as Amazon to directly employ delivery drivers rather than relying on subcontractors.“I’ve been talking to many of the small businesses,” Wong told the New York Post. “If this bill gets passed, it will close a lot of them and that’s bad for my district.”What the bill doesCouncilwoman Tiffany Cabán introduced the bill in 2025, and Wong signed on as a co-sponsor. After she reintroduced it this year, he supported it again. The legislation would end Amazon’s reliance on subcontractors by requiring it to obtain licences for its 15 last-mile facilities in the city and to hire delivery workers directly as full-time employees. Other companies, including FedEx, would face the same rules. According to Amazon, the bill would affect more than 5,000 delivery workers employed by about 40 third-party contractors. Amazon doesn’t directly employ delivery drivers anywhere in the US. It has threatened to close its New York last-mile warehouses and lay off about 2,000 workers there if the bill passes. An AKFR study commissioned by Amazon estimates that delivery costs for New Yorkers would rise by $664 a year, or about $5.20 a package.The Teamsters union, which strongly backs the bill, accuses Amazon of union-busting and of using the subcontracting model to dodge responsibility for worker and street safety. The union says Amazon has spent more than $5 million on a campaign against the bill.Amazon warns of warehouse closuresAmazon has strongly opposed the bill and has warned that it could shut down its last-mile warehouses in New York City if the legislation becomes law. The company has said such a move could result in the loss of about 2,000 warehouse jobs. The e-commerce giant also argues that consumers could face higher costs. A study commissioned by Amazon and conducted by AKFR estimated that New Yorkers' delivery costs could rise by an average of $664 annually, or roughly $5.20 per package, if the proposal is enacted.One unnamed council member who supports the bill's objectives but remains concerned about its consequences told the Post that many lawmakers may not fully understand the proposal's impact.“I agree with the intent of the bill to protect workers, but I’m concerned about people losing their jobs and the sponsor doesn’t deny that people will lose their jobs,” the council member said.Pressure on council membersOne of the bill’s 35 current co-sponsors, who asked not to be named, told the Post there is “tremendous political pressure” and that many colleagues, including the speaker, don’t fully understand the bill’s ramifications. The member agreed with its intent to protect workers but said the sponsor doesn’t deny that jobs will be lost. Wong’s chief of staff, Daniel Kurzyna, said the Teamsters called his office within minutes of the name being removed in September. “They noticed fast,” he said, adding that the union has called regularly since asking Wong to reconsider.Menin under pressure to schedule a voteRep. Ro Khanna, a California Democrat who is considering a 2028 presidential run, urged Council Speaker Julie Menin to schedule a vote, writing on X that delivery workers deserve safe and fair conditions. Menin, a centrist, has not taken a position on the bill. She has voiced concern that it could cause job losses and lead Amazon to raise prices. Mamdani and Teamsters members rallied at City Hall on October 22, urging her to call a vote immediately. Menin says the bill is being reviewed by the city’s Law Department, according to a spokesperson, who said she remains committed to legislation that protects workers and keeps the jobs in New York. Sources told the Post the Law Department is examining whether the bill violates the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act of 1994, which bars states from regulating the price, route or service of motor carriers. New York would be the first US city to adopt such a measure.Legal questions also under reviewBeyond the political debate, the bill faces legal scrutiny. According to the New York Post report, New York City's Law Department is examining whether the proposal could conflict with the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act of 1994, which limits states and local governments from enacting regulations related to the prices, routes or services of motor carriers. Speaker Julie Menin has not publicly endorsed or opposed the legislation but has expressed concerns that it could lead to job losses and higher costs for consumers. Her office said the bill remains under review and continues to move through the legislative process.The latest development highlights growing divisions within New York City's Democratic leadership as officials weigh worker protections against warnings from businesses that stricter regulations could prompt companies such as Amazon to scale back operations in the city.You use AI every day. articles.title: Popular cooking methods may destroy key health benefits of broccoli, experts warn
articles.summary: Boiling broccoli drains vitamin C and glucoraphanin, but chopping florets 30 to 40 minutes before cooking may help preserve cancer-fighting compounds.
articles.body: Not all methods of cooking broccoli are created equal, and some simple tips can ensure you get the most nutrients out of it. Whether it's steamed, roasted or added to a stir-fry, broccoli is a healthy option packed with vitamins such as A, C and K, minerals such as calcium, potassium and iron, fiber and even a potentially cancer-fighting compound, The Washington Post recently reported. But certain ways of cooking broccoli can ensure you get the most out of the cruciferous vegetable and preserve those compounds. YOU'RE PROBABLY COOKING RICE WRONG, AND CHEFS REVEAL THE SIMPLE MISTAKE TO AVOID Boiling broccoli can cause water-soluble nutrients and compounds to leach into the cooking water, while prolonged or high-heat cooking, including roasting, can reduce antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cancer-fighting properties. "Boiling causes the most loss in nutrients," Sol Figueroa, a Florida-based registered dietitian nutritionist with Mochi Health, told Fox News Digital. "Vitamin C and glucoraphanin dissolve in water, so a lot of them end up in the cooking water that gets poured down the drain." NATURAL COMPOUND IN BLUEBERRIES AND GRAPES MAY UNLOCK FAT-BURNING PROCESS IN MUSCLE CELLS Glucoraphanin is a natural compound found in cruciferous vegetables and, when it is digested, it can be converted into sulforaphane, a compound studied for potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects and possible benefits for liver, metabolic and gut health, as well as cancer prevention. Figueroa offered several tips to help get the most out of your broccoli. One way to preserve some of the nutrients is to use as little water as possible when boiling, she said. Another is to sprinkle mustard powder on cooked broccoli. Mustard seeds contain myrosinase, an enzyme that helps convert glucoraphanin to sulforaphane and that can be lost during cooking. COMMON GRILLING MISTAKE COULD STRIP FISH OF KEY NUTRIENTS AND RUIN YOUR MEAL, EXPERTS WARN Some simple prep also may help preserve sulforaphane, according to Figueroa. "We can't say broccoli prevents disease, but the findings are promising." "Chopping the broccoli and letting it sit for about 30 to 40 minutes before cooking gives sulforaphane time to form first," she said. FOUR COMMON KITCHEN HABITS THAT CHEFS SAY HOME COOKS NEED TO STOP DOING IMMEDIATELY Most of the research related to broccoli's health claims has been conducted in labs and animals, Figueroa added. "We can't say broccoli prevents disease, but the findings are promising," she said. Steaming is one of the best ways to preserve broccoli's enzymes, and while the method often reduces vitamin C in other foods, research shows broccoli might be an exception, the Washington Post reported. Quickly microwaving broccoli may help preserve nutrients, according to the outlet, and using broccoli's cooking water in soup or stew can help retain some water-soluble vitamins. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Felice Kaufman, a Florida-based food blogger at Cooking in the Keys and former New York Whole Foods Market chef, said she usually steams broccoli, cutting the florets into similar sizes and checking for doneness after about three minutes. "Taste a piece. If you'd eat it right then, take it out of the pot," Kaufman told Fox News Digital. "The heat keeps cooking the broccoli after it comes out of the pot." Kaufman also recommends using the stalk, which she trims, slices and cooks with the florets. "The stalk is the best part," she said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES She prefers steaming to boiling, in part to preserve vitamin C, but said that's not always possible. "If the sink is full — it happens — I'll throw the broccoli straight into the boiling water," she said. "One less thing to wash." No matter how it's served, getting some broccoli into your diet is key, experts agree. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "The most important thing is eating broccoli at all," Figueroa said. If roasting is the way your family likes it best, do that, she added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kaufman echoed that advice, saying, "Five ounces of broccoli, organic, conventional or frozen, is better than any processed food you can eat."

articles.title: Tinned food and bottled water sales jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
articles.summary: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
articles.body:
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.

Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.

"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.

"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.

Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign.

Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions".

The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

articles.title: Couple deny embezzling £138,000 from dying boy's fundraiser
articles.summary: It is alleged they embezzled the money while acting as administrators of a GoFundMe set up for Nathaniel Nabena.
articles.body:
A Scottish couple have appeared in court accused of embezzling £138,482 from a fundraiser set up to help a dying boy.

Prosecutors allege Sharyn and Mark McInally-Johnston embezzled the money while acting as organisers and administrators of a GoFundMe set up for Nathaniel Nabena by his father.

Nathaniel, from Nigeria, died from an infection in 2022, a year after receiving a stem-cell transplant.

The couple, aged 40 and 45 respectively, denied the charge during an appearance at Dundee Sheriff Court.

It is alleged the couple, from Kenmore in Perthshire, embezzled the money between May 2021 and January 2024.

The offence is said to have taken place at addresses in Helensburgh, Aberfeldy, and elsewhere.

The court was told that the trial was likely to hear evidence from seven witnesses, including five police officers.

The case was continued to a trial at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court on 22 February.

Nathaniel was initially ineligible for NHS-funded treatment as he was a non-EU citizen.

A newspaper campaign to raise funds was backed by celebrities including Simon Cowell.

But an application to stay in the UK on compassionate grounds was later granted, allowing Nathaniel to receive the treatment.

articles.title: GCC agrees to set up advanced military command headquarters in Kuwait
articles.summary: Gulf leaders emphasised the need to strengthen defence coordination to confront present and future regional challenges.
articles.body:
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has agreed to set up an advanced headquarters for its Unified Military Command in Kuwait, with plans to station “appropriate” military forces there.

The announcement by the GCC’s General Secretariat on Tuesday followed a meeting of defence ministers from member states in Bahrain.

“The leaders of the GCC states – may God protect and preserve them – consistently emphasise the necessity and importance of strengthening this blessed Gulf journey, enabling it to confront various challenges and threats, both present and future,” the group said in a statement.

Details about the headquarters and the number or type of troops expected to be deployed have yet to be disclosed. The GCC consists of six United States-allied Gulf states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

Established at a summit in Kuwait in December 2013, the GCC’s Unified Military Command was designed to oversee joint military operations and enhance collective defence against threats to member states’ territory, airspace, maritime areas and interests.

Most Gulf countries host major US military installations and were targeted in Iranian missile and drone attacks in the weeks after the US-Israel war on Iran began on February 28.

The ‌‌‌‌war has disrupted air travel and shipping, and raised concerns over the security of the ‌‌‌‌region’s ‌‌‌‌vital oil and gas exports.

The Iran war has also reignited the conflict in Yemen, where escalating fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government has further plunged the region into uncertainty, following the collapse in July of a United Nations-brokered ceasefire largely in place since 2022.

The Houthis have also targeted sites across Saudi Arabia, including the capital Riyadh.

Last month, an attack by the armed group on the city’s King Khalid international airport killed 14 people and wounded more than 300 others, in the deadliest assault on the kingdom in more than a decade.

articles.title: The unseen casualties of Iran war: How deadly attacks at sea are putting sailors' lives at risk
articles.summary: The Iran war is turning one of the world's busiest shipping corridors into a graveyard of unanswered distress calls, missing vessels and mounting
articles.body: The Iran war is turning one of the world's busiest shipping corridors into a graveyard of unanswered distress calls, missing vessels and mounting casualties.At least 25 seafarers have been killed and 130 maritime incidents reported since the conflict began on February 28. The disappearance of two cargo ships carrying six crew members, including two Indians, has exposed the growing human cost of a war being fought far beyond the battlefield.According to a Reuters investigation, commercial shipping has been caught between two fronts, with Iran attacking vessels in an effort to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz, while the United States has struck Iran-linked ships as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.The attacks have disrupted maritime operations and exposed civilian crews to the dangers of a conflict in which even ships with no direct military role are increasingly at risk.The scale of the danger is reflected in the disappearance of two cargo vessels, Bridge 1 and Bridge 2, which were last detected in Iranian waters on May 9.The ships, both flying the Bolivian flag and reportedly carrying steel as part of Iranian trade, lost communication with their crews near Iran's Kish Island. Their last known Automatic Identification System (AIS) transmission placed them around eight nautical miles from the island at 4.50 pm. No distress signals were received, and neither vessel appeared on the IMO's list of reported incidents, Reuters reported.Twenty-three-year-old Naveen Kumar from Tamil Nadu is among those missing after the vessels disappeared. According to Reuters, Kumar had signed a six-month contract for what his family believed was a Dubai-based job but was taken to Iran within a week of joining. His family has not heard from him since May 9.His mother, V Pandiselvi, told Reuters that the family has been desperately seeking information about his whereabouts. She said they continue to replay his old voice messages while waiting for news. The family had also borrowed around Rs 15 lakh to finance his maritime training.The uncertainty has left Kumar's family struggling to establish what happened to him. His family approached Mumbai-based recruitment firm Lascar Marine Services, which had arranged his employment. However, they alleged that the company initially assured them of his return but later stopped responding to their calls.India's Seamen's Employment Office subsequently withdrew the firm's recruitment licence and barred its past and present directors from maritime business for five years, citing failures to repatriate seafarers, including Kumar, and pay their wages.The uncertainty extends beyond the Indian sailor. The six crew members aboard the two missing vessels included three Iraqis, two Indians and one Pakistani.Iraqi maritime official Khaled Saad al-Thaalibi told Reuters that Iranian search-and-rescue teams had looked for the vessels but failed to find them."We don't know if the vessels sunk or were confiscated by a country," he said. Shipping sources have also raised the possibility of a US strike, but the circumstances surrounding their disappearance remain unconfirmed.The disappearance of the vessels has also raised questions about the safety of commercial ships operating in the region.Reuters reported that the two ships were not included in the IMO's record of maritime incidents, despite their disappearance and the missing crew. articles.title: Police assess new reports against Russell Brand after his rape conviction
articles.summary: British police said that detectives were assessing a number of new reports about actor and comedian Russell Brand in the wake of his jailing for rape.
articles.body: British police said on Tuesday that detectives were assessing a number of new reports about actor and comedian Russell Brand in the wake of his jailing for rape and sexual assaults. Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and a Hollywood film star, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years on Monday after being convicted of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009. The 51-year-old former husband of American pop star Katy Perry, who in recent years moved away from the mainstream, had denied all the charges and said he had never had non-consensual sex. After he was found guilty, detectives said they were investigating two other allegations of rape, one involving a then 16-year-old girl, and London’s police chief they expected more women to come forward. Police said others had now done so. “Several people have contacted the investigation team during and since the trial to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation,” a police spokesperson said. “Detectives are assessing this information as part of their ongoing enquiries.” A former girlfriend of Brand, Jemima Goldsmith, wrote on X on Monday that she had called the police about him during an altercation at her house in 2014, but had not pressed any charges. “I am glad and relieved that Russell Brand has finally faced justice,” she said. Brand rose to prominence in Britain hosting a spin-off show to “Big Brother” on Channel 4. During the 2000s, he became a regular fixture on television and radio, and went on to star in a number of films such as “Get Him to the Greek.” In 2010 he married Perry, a relationship that he told his trial had brought him “staggering fame.” The marriage ended after 14 months.

articles.title: Investigators recover the voice recorder from a jet crash in Florida that killed 9
articles.summary: Investigators said Monday they have recovered the cockpit voice recorder from a business jet that plummeted from the sky amid severe weather in Florida last week, killing all nine people on board.
articles.body: Investigators said Monday they have recovered the cockpit voice recorder from a business jet that plummeted from the sky amid severe weather in Florida last week, killing all nine people on board. The recorder was found at the site where the Bahamas-bound Learjet slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball Nov. 1, the National Transportation Safety Board said in a statement posted to social media. If data from the device can be recovered, it could provide crucial details about what the pilots said to each other as they encountered turbulence, ice formed on the wings and they lost control of the aircraft. It was not immediately known if the recorder had been damaged or if it was working in the first place. The NTSB said the device was being evaluated at a lab in Washington. From photos the agency posted online, showing the recorder’s orange-painted metal shell, it appeared to be in decent shape, aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti told The Associated Press. “It’s very plausible that any info on the recorder survived,” Guzzetti said. “If they can recover it, and it’s from the accident flight, that will be a huge help to investigators.” He noted that when the NTSB recovered the cockpit voice recorder from a medical transport plane that crashed in Philadelphia in January 2025, killing seven people, it turned out the device likely had not been functioning for several years. Witnesses captured dramatic video as the business jet plunged nose-first into the ground, and air traffic control transmissions recorded the disturbing moments as the pilots realized their fate. But the cockpit voice recorder could shed light on other aspects of the crash, including why the Learjet appeared to steer around a large storm cell only to head directly into a rapidly developing smaller one. Investigators have said pieces of a key part of the tail called the elevator, which controls the plane’s pitch, were found more than a mile away from the main crater, confirming the plane started to break apart before impact. The co-pilot told air traffic controllers that the plane was being thrown up and down more than 700 feet (213 meters), and she asked them for a better route through the area. Generally, it takes 12 to 18 months for the NTSB to complete a crash investigation, but complicated cases can take longer. The NTSB’s roughly 400 workers are pursuing more than 1,200 active investigations. Investigators will review maintenance records and any history of problems with the plane. They will also interview officials at Upper Jets, the company that operated the flight, as well as air traffic controllers and people who work at the airport in Austin, Texas, from where the plane departed.

articles.title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as leaders compete to form government
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
articles.body:
Israel's new parliament will be sworn in on Tuesday, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The former army chief was tasked with forming a government by the president, after he received the backing of 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared to 46 for Netanyahu.

But Eisenkot faces an uphill struggle. His bloc of four parties won 48 seats in last month's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.

Almost half of the MKs being sworn in did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.

The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months.

One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition.

On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government.

Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office.

This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps".

Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities.

The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners.

The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue.

The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do.

Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation.

The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside.

If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs.

In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc.

Netanyahu - Israel's longest-serving leader - reiterated in a video on Monday his call for the formation of a government of national unity, which he said he would lead as prime minister.

He said any Zionist party - those which support Israel as a Jewish state - including opposition parties, would be eligible. He warned against a government which relied on what he called "the Islamists", an apparent reference to Arab parties.

"You cannot form a government with Hamas supporters," he said.

articles.title: A 61-year-old Michigan woman thought her $30 scratch-off ticket had won $5,000, but a phone scan revealed a $2 million prize; she chose about $1.3 million in cash and plans to buy homes in Michigan and Florida
articles.summary: An Ingham County woman went from celebrating what she thought was a modest lottery win to discovering she had won a life-changing $2 million (£1.54
articles.body: An Ingham County woman went from celebrating what she thought was a modest lottery win to discovering she had won a life-changing $2 million (£1.54 million) jackpot after scanning her ticket. The 61-year-old woman, who chose to remain anonymous, bought her winning $30 scratch-off ticket for the Michigan Lottery's $2,000,000 Cashword instant game at the Holt Express convenience store at 2196 West Delhi Avenue in Holt. This was confirmed in an official release published on the Michigan Lottery Connect platform. When she first checked her ticket, she thought she had won a good amount of money. However, the actual prize was much larger than she had expected.Misread ticket reveals million-dollar prize"I scratched off my ticket and thought I won $5,000," the player told Michigan Lottery officials when she claimed her prize. "I scanned it on the lottery app to double check, and when $2 million popped up on the screen, I was in utter shock. My husband and I couldn't believe it." The winner recently visited Michigan Lottery headquarters in Lansing to collect her prize. She had two options: receive the full $2 million through yearly payments or take a smaller amount in one payment. She chose the one-time cash payment of approximately $1.3 million, local news outlet WILX-TV reported. The $1.3 million lump-sum payment reflects the state and federal taxes that are withheld from large lottery prizes in the United States.Real estate plans in two statesNow that she has secured her winnings, the woman already has plans for how to spend the money. "I plan to use my winnings to buy a home in Michigan, a home in Florida, and then save the rest," she said during her interview with lottery officials. Her plan to spend time in both Michigan and Florida follows a common choice among Midwestern residents known as "snowbirds." Many people in this group spend the winter months in warmer southern states while keeping a home near their families in the Midwest.Local store handles winning saleThe Holt Express store that sold the winning ticket is in Ingham County, about 10 miles south of downtown Lansing. In Michigan, local stores that sell tickets worth top lottery prizes usually receive an extra commission from the state lottery commission for selling a winning jackpot ticket. According to the Michigan Lottery, the $2,000,000 Cashword game launched in August 2024. Each ticket costs $30 and gives players a chance to win prizes ranging from $30 to the top jackpot of $2 million. Since the game launched, players have won more than $22 million in prizes. Each ticket includes several crossword-style word puzzles. Players can win cash prizes by completing specific word combinations.Michigan Lottery records show that the $2,000,000 Cashword scratch-off remains one of the state's most popular $30 lottery ticket options. Several top prizes have been won at stores across Michigan's Lower Peninsula since the game first launched. For the 61-year-old winner, scanning her ticket a second time with the mobile app made all the difference. What she first believed was a $5,000 win turned out to be a life-changing amount of money.
